notes:
Quick summary: AdeptFlow builds an IDE copilot integrated into VSCode and JetBrains editors. Primary ask = low-latency streaming with tight first-token latency (TTFT) and predictable in-editor experience. Team is highly sensitive to jitter; developers report that even occasional 200-300ms spikes kill flow. They want token-budget strategies per file and per-repo to control cost.

Key requirements / paraphrased quotes:
- "TTFT <= 120ms for first token in small completions (20-80 tokens) on fast networks"
- "Jitter should be < 30ms stdev for streaming payloads; otherwise UI blinks and suggestions are ignored"
- Per-cursor token budget (default 512, configurable up to 2048) and graceful backpressure when budget exhausted
- Version pinning for model families per feature (completion vs. explain) + deterministic fallback rules

Technical interest areas discussed: continuous streaming with prefix caching, KV cache warmup for common repo prefixes, adaptive token budgeting (reduce sample length when latency rises), client-side debounce + partial-response stitching, and using Redwood Optimize suggestions for batching thresholds. They are open to Hosted API for POC but prefer Dedicated for predictable tail latency at scale.

Security/compliance notes: SOC2 required for production; SSO/SAML for SSO; EU data residency for some enterprise customers. Legal asked for KMS/HSM options.

Notes style: fragments, follow-ups, next steps captured below. SE suggested a perf harness (ts-client simulator) to reproduce jitter in CI and run TTFT histograms.

Week 1: implement streaming client + partial stitching, add token-budget config UI
Week 2: run TTFT/jitter benchmarks (TS simulator), collect histograms and traces, iterate on batching config

Scale canary to 500 devs if TTFT 95th pct < 150ms and jitter stdev < 30ms
perf_targets: TTFT (median) <= 120ms on standard dev laptop + home broadband
95th pct TTFT <= 200ms for hosted POC; <=150ms for Dedicated
Token budget controls: default 512 tokens, throttle/backpressure policy when >80% consumed
Cost target: average token cost per session <$0.02 for completions under 120 tokens
integration_notes: Prefer server-side pinning: completion routes -> quantized code model v1.2; explainability routes -> higher-quality float model
Client SDK to support incremental streaming + resumable partials for flaky networks
Add local debounce (50ms) + server-side prefetch for common repo prefixes
Deployment preference: POC on Hosted API, move to Dedicated for SLA and tail latency control
Need Redwood Optimize recommendations for batching thresholds (suggested 4-8 request batches under IDE workloads)
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Occasional high tail latency caused by cold KV cache -> Mitigation: pre-warm KV cache on editor open for common repo prefixes
Risk: Token churn on long editing sessions increases cost -> Mitigation: enforce per-file token budget and dynamic summarization to reduce context
Risk: Jitter on developer home networks -> Mitigation: client-side smoothing + partial incremental tokens to keep UI responsive
Risk: Legal/HQ EU residency requirement -> Mitigation: offer region pinning and Dedicated in EU region
